sentences.text: The type species is Spinosaurus aegyptiacus, a name meaning 'spine lizard' that combines Latin and Greek roots for spine and lizard.
It possessed a long, low, narrow skull resembling a modern crocodilian, equipped with straight conical teeth that had few to no serrations.
Distinctive neural spines extending from its vertebrae grew to at least 1.65 meters long, likely forming a sail-like structure covered in skin.
A 2022 study suggests Spinosaurus aegyptiacus could have reached 14 meters in length and 7.4 metric tons in body mass.
Since its discovery, Spinosaurus has been considered a contender for the largest theropod dinosaur.
Ernst Stromer described Spinosaurus in 1915 after it was first discovered in Egypt in 1912.
Spinosaurus may have first been discovered in October 1898 when Fernand Foureau found two teeth in southern Algeria.
In 2008, a Moroccan fossil collector presented fragmentary fossils to Nizar Ibrahim, who suspected they belonged to Spinosaurus.
Spinosaurus is known to have fed on both aquatic and terrestrial prey.
Evidence suggests Spinosaurus was semiaquatic, though the extent of its swimming ability is strongly contested.
Multiple functions have been proposed for the dorsal sail of Spinosaurus, including thermoregulation and display to intimidate rivals or attract mates.
Ernst Stromer originally named the clade Spinosauridae to include only Spinosaurus.
Some researchers, such as Alfred Romer, proposed that Acrocanthosaurus and Altispinax belonged to Spinosauridae due to their tall neural spines, though later studies rejected this.
Spinosaurus lived in North Africa during the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 100 to 94 million years ago.
It inhabited a wet environment of marshes and mangroves alongside other dinosaurs, as well as fish, crocodylomorphs, lizards, turtles, pterosaurs, and plesiosaurs.
It is unclear whether the fossils represent one or two distinct species of Spinosaurus.
The validity of Sigilmassasaurus, S. maroccanus, and Oxalaia as distinct taxa from Spinosaurus is debated.
Many studies have proposed that fossils assigned to Spinosaurus or Sigilmassasaurus actually belong to other dinosaur groups like iguanodonts or carcharodontosaurids.
Some researchers differentiated Spinosaurus maroccanus from S. aegyptiacus based on the ratio of centrum length to posterior articular facet height in neck vertebrae.
